resource_sampling.mechanism: experiments/b5/run_b5.py --mode sample-only + ResourceSampler class (Windows stdlib ctypes: QueryInformationProcess peak memory / cumulative CPU + GlobalMemoryStatusEx available memory; 10 s sampling interval by default; thread-based, failures recorded as notes, never abort training)

metric_definitions.process_peak_memory_bytes: Windows PROCESS_PERF_INFO.PeakWorkingSetSize (monotonic high-water mark of this process, bytes)
metric_definitions.process_cpu_seconds_total: cumulative kernel+user CPU seconds of this process since start (QueryInformationProcess HighestUserTimer+HighestKernelTimer)
metric_definitions.avg_process_cpu_percent_of_one_core: (total CPU seconds / window wall-clock seconds) * 100; >100 possible on multi-core
metric_definitions.system_available_memory_bytes_min: minimum observed GlobalMemoryStatusEx.ullAvailPhys across samples (instantaneous readings, not a true minimum guarantee)

sampling_policy.window: starts immediately before Trainer.train(), stops immediately after; default interval 10 s; one extra point at window end
sampling_policy.failure_handling: per-tick exceptions recorded in the point and in report.notes; unavailable APIs -> null metrics with explicit note; sampling NEVER aborts or alters training or the fail-closed B5 stop logic
sampling_policy.guarantees: no metric is fabricated: unavailable = null, never 0

tests/test_b5_fault_injection_isolated.py (11 tests: hard-stop termination; 5 anomaly tokens pause; write-failure fail-closed; resume rejection on checksum/step/vocab/seq_len; hard-stop never resumable; counters preserved + no checkpoint at pause step; 9-field schema; source-checkpoint-untouched proof)

fault_injection.kind: controlled fault injection (isolated tmp_path + mocked evaluate) -- NOT natural real-training faults

scenarios.name: hard-stop termination
scenarios.trigger: mocked evaluator returns loss=9.9 (>= hard threshold) for 2 consecutive evals (consecutive_count=2)
scenarios.expected: summary.stopped=='hard_stop', steps_executed==2, 9-field state written, no checkpoint_step2.pt

scenarios.name: anomaly pause (all 5 tokens)
scenarios.expected: summary.stopped==token, anomaly state written, no checkpoint at anomaly step

scenarios.name: state-write failure fail-closed
scenarios.trigger: pause_state_path whose parent is a FILE (mkdir fails -> save returns False)
scenarios.expected: training stops (summary.stopped set), no checkpoint, no fallback file, blocker file untouched

scenarios.name: resume rejected: config checksum mismatch
scenarios.trigger: anomaly state written under config A; fresh trainer with config B (different vocab)

scenarios.name: resume rejected: vocab_size mismatch
scenarios.trigger: state under vocab=32, resume trainer vocab=16

scenarios.name: resume rejected: max_seq_len mismatch
scenarios.trigger: state under seq_len=8, resume trainer seq_len=16

scenarios.name: hard-stop never resumable
scenarios.trigger: hard_stop state on disk; resume_from_pause on a fresh trainer
scenarios.expected: False, counters of the new trainer untouched

scenarios.name: paused counters preserved + no checkpoint
scenarios.trigger: step 1 ok (low loss clears counters), step 2 nan anomaly
scenarios.expected: state.warn_consec==0/hard_consec==0 at step 2, checkpoint_step1.pt exists, checkpoint_step2.pt absent

scenarios.name: 9-field schema (no 10th)
scenarios.expected: key set == ALL_FIELDS (6 required + 3 optional), model_checkpoint_path / validation_error_summary absent

fault_injection.side_effect_check: every scenario runs inside a fresh pytest tmp_path; test_source_checkpoint_untouched_after_module re-hashes the step-350 source checkpoint after the module and asserts it equals the known SHA-256
fault_injection.limitations: these are isolated, mocked fault injections. They prove the control flow, state protocol and side-effect boundaries, but they are NOT natural faults occurring inside a real 100-step training run; no real run has ever triggered a hard-stop or anomaly
